title: The Clear Spring
text: A spring in a white grove, its water so clear it seems not to be there at all. Old bones lie curled on the moss all around it, the remains of people who drank and stayed young, then simply stayed. Some of the skulls still have all their teeth, smiling.

options.label: The most weathered of you drinks from the spring, tempted by the years it promises back.

outcomes.text: Years fall away from them. They feel it in every joint, and they do not want to stop drinking.
They want to stay. They lie down among the smiling bones; it takes three of you to drag them away.

options.label: Bottle some for home, and leave the drinking to the dead.

outcomes.text: The water never goes stale, though it never quite stays still in the bottle.

options.label: Leave the spring to its dead. Youth that keeps you forever is no gift.

outcomes.text: The bones watch you go, not unkindly. The spring's chill settles on you anyway, closing your wounds.
The bones watch you go. That night everyone dreams of drinking and wakes thirsty.
